question: Should OpenClaw core permanently support the proposed local, container, reverse-proxy, and node-mode profiles—with hosting.profile, startup flags/environment variables, runtime identity, and plugin-contributed readiness criteria—as a release-tested support matrix?
rationale: Tests can establish correctness and upgrade behavior, but they cannot decide whether these named deployment postures and new public configuration/SDK contracts belong in core or should remain downstream compositions over generic readiness.

options.title: Adopt the core matrix
options.body: Approve the four opt-in profiles and public readiness contract, land the generic readiness prerequisite first, then review the reduced profile-only diff.

options.title: Keep readiness generic
options.body: Land only canonical selectable readiness and ask downstream hosts to compose deployment-specific criteria without permanent named profiles in core.

options.title: Narrow the matrix
options.body: Approve only the profiles with an immediate maintained support commitment and defer the remaining postures to a later RFC or downstream integration.

recommendation.title: Adopt the core matrix
recommendation.body: Approve the four opt-in profiles and public readiness contract, land the generic readiness prerequisite first, then review the reduced profile-only diff.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository contributor map explicitly routes Core, CLI, Gateway, and Security work to this area, covering the product and compatibility decision.
